summary: Well-executed, preregistered, artifact-backed paired study that isolates verifier+single-repair impact under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Execution and archival artifacts are comprehensive and reproducible. A single outstanding provenance/verifiability defect remains: the manuscript omits the deterministic identifier and a short artifact-backed summary of the one discordant episode (baseline fail → guarded pass). This prevents immediate deterministic audit of the corrective event despite the archived raw results. Otherwise the prior requested clarifications (per-cluster counts and exact-test formula) appear addressed in the manuscript and artifacts.
critical_issues: Manuscript does not include the deterministic identifier (pair/episode id) of the single discordant episode where the guarded arm converted a baseline failure to a pass, nor a concise artifact-backed summary of the validator-reported violation class and the repair that was applied. This omission reduces immediate verifiability despite the archived raw_results.jsonl.
required_revisions: Insert the deterministic identifier (pair id present in execution/raw_results.jsonl) for the discordant episode into the manuscript and, using the archived validator_trace and repair_provider_trace, add a short sanitized summary of: (a) the violation class/severity reported by the verifier on the baseline shared candidate, and (b) the repair action and final validator outcome. (All details must be sourced from the archived artifacts; no new analyses required.)

Explicitly state whether the realized per-cluster sample sizes match the preregistered allocation (167/167/166) and, if so, cite the execution/task_manifest.jsonl path or artifact entry that confirms the realized counts; if any deterministic deviation occurred, document it and point to the manifest evidence.
optional_revisions: Add a small table or one-paragraph appendix (sourced from analysis artifacts) showing per-violation-class counts and any attempted repairs by class to help readers assess where the lone failure arose.

Briefly quantify model-call cost and latency trade-offs implied by the observed model_calls_used = 501 and repair-stage calls = 1 to contextualize shared_initial_candidate vs regeneration-based guarded workflows (artifacts contain timestamps and call counts).

Add one or two explicit citations and brief comparisons to the closest empirical generate→verify→repair studies in Related Work to sharpen novelty positioning (use the verified bibliography entries already archived).
